\section{A Comprehensive Guide to Directed Evolution of Self-Modifying AI Agents}

\hrule
\section{Abstract}

\textbf{WAFT} (Wave Agent Framework & Tools) is a Python framework for directed evolution of self-modifying AI agents. Unlike traditional agent frameworks that execute fixed code, WAFT enables agents to write, modify, and evolve their own Python source code through a process of mutation and natural selection. The framework serves as a scientific instrument for studying the physics of artificial cognition, with complete lineage tracking, fitness evaluation, and telemetry systems designed to produce rigorous data for research publication.

\textbf{Core Promise}: "Don't just build agents. Breed them."

This enhanced handbook provides comprehensive documentation with detailed architecture diagrams, fitness metrics analysis, evolution cycle visualizations, case studies, and technical specifications. Whether you're a researcher studying artificial cognition, a developer building self-improving systems, or a scientist tracking evolutionary lineages, this handbook serves as your complete guide to the WAFT ecosystem.

\hrule
\section{1. Introduction}

\subsection{1.1 What is WAFT?}

WAFT is a \textbf{scientific instrument} for studying the physics of artificial cognition through directed evolution. It provides:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Self-Modifying Agents}: Agents that write and modify their own Python code
\item \textbf{Evolutionary Framework}: Mutation, selection, and reproduction mechanisms
\item \textbf{Fitness Evaluation}: Scint System (Reality Fracture Detection) as natural selection
\item \textbf{Complete Telemetry}: Flight Recorder for phylogenetic tree reconstruction
\item \textbf{Scientific Data}: Publication-ready lineage tracking and analysis
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Differentiators}:

\begin{longtable}{lll}
\toprule
\textbf{Feature} & \textbf{Traditional Frameworks} & \textbf{WAFT} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
Code Modification & Static, fixed code & Dynamic, self-modifying \\
Evolution & None & Genetic improvement \\
Fitness Testing & Manual & Automated Scint Gym \\
Lineage Tracking & None & Complete phylogenetic trees \\
Scientific Data & Limited & Publication-ready \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{1.2 The Scientific Mission}

WAFT is built to produce data for research on \textbf{"The Physics of Artificial Cognition."} The system enables:

\begin{itemize}
\item Tracking complete evolutionary lineages (phylogenetic trees)
\item Measuring fitness through rigorous testing (Scint Gym)
\item Recording all mutations with complete context (Flight Recorder)
\item Enabling scientific analysis of agent evolution
\end{itemize}

\textbf{The Ultimate Goal}: Observe a "God-Head" agent emerge from thousands of generations of directed mutation.

\textbf{Research Applications}:
\begin{itemize}
\item Evolutionary algorithm studies
\item Artificial cognition research
\item Agent architecture analysis
\item Fitness landscape mapping
\item Convergence pattern identification
\end{itemize}

\subsection{1.3 Core Philosophy}

WAFT embodies four key principles:

1. \textbf{Scientific}: Produces rigorous data for research publication
2. \textbf{Evolutionary}: Agents evolve through genetic improvement, not just execution
3. \textbf{Observable}: Every action recorded in the Flight Recorder for analysis
4. \textbf{Directed}: Evolution guided by fitness functions, not random mutation

\textbf{Philosophical Foundation}:

The framework is built on the principle that \textbf{code is DNA} - agent source code and configuration represent the genetic material that determines behavior and capabilities. Through directed mutation and natural selection (via the Scint System), agents evolve toward improved fitness, creating a complete evolutionary record suitable for scientific analysis.

\hrule
\section{2. The Three Pillars}

WAFT's architecture rests on three fundamental pillars that enable directed evolution. Each pillar provides essential functionality for the evolutionary process.

\subsection{2.1 Pillar 1: The Substrate (Code as DNA)}

\textbf{Agents write their own Python source code.}

In WAFT, code is DNA. Every agent has a unique \textbf{genome} represented by:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Genome ID}: SHA-256 hash of agent's code + configuration
\item \textbf{Mutations}: Code changes, config updates, prompt evolution
\item \textbf{Evolution}: Hot-swapping better genomes mid-execution
\item \textbf{Reproduction}: Creating child agents with specific genetic modifications
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Genome Structure}:

The genome consists of multiple components that together form the agent's complete genetic identity:

\begin{longtable}{lll}
\toprule
\textbf{Component} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Hash Contribution} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
Source Code & Python implementation & Primary \\
Configuration & Agent settings, parameters & Primary \\
Prompt Template & System/user prompts & Secondary \\
Dependencies & Required packages & Secondary \\
Metadata & Version, author, description & Tertiary \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Genome ID Calculation}:
\begin{lstlisting}
Genome ID = SHA-256(
    source_code + 
    config_json + 
    prompt_template + 
    dependencies_list
)
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Key Operations}:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Spawn}: Create variants with mutations
\end{itemize}
  - Generates new genome with modifications
  - Calculates new genome ID
  - Records parent-child relationship
  - Initializes in SPAWNING state

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Evolve}: Adopt better genomes
\end{itemize}
  - Compares fitness scores
  - Hot-swaps code/config
  - Updates genome ID
  - Records evolution event

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Reproduce}: Create children with genetic modifications
\end{itemize}
  - Inherits parent genome
  - Applies specified mutations
  - Creates new genome ID
  - Establishes lineage chain

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Hot-Swap}: Replace code/config during execution
\end{itemize}
  - Validates new genome
  - Updates runtime state
  - Records mutation event
  - Maintains execution continuity

\textbf{Example}:
\begin{lstlisting}
# Agent spawns a variant with improved prompt
agent.spawn_variant(mutation={
    "prompt": "improved_prompt.json",
    "code_changes": ["optimized_loop.py"]
})

# Agent evolves into fittest variant
agent.evolve(target_genome_id="abc123...")

# Agent reproduces with specific mutation
child = agent.reproduce(mutation={
    "optimization_level": "high",
    "error_handling": "strict"
})
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Mutation Types}:

\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Type} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Impact} & \textbf{Reversibility} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
Code Change & Python source modification & High & Partial \\
Config Update & Parameter adjustment & Medium & Full \\
Prompt Evolution & Instruction refinement & Medium & Full \\
Dependency Change & Package addition/removal & High & Full \\
Architecture Shift & Structural reorganization & Very High & Difficult \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{2.2 Pillar 2: The Physics (Scint System)}

\textbf{Reality Fracture Detection acts as natural selection.}

The \textbf{Scint System} (Scint Gym) serves as the fitness function that tests agents on four types of errors:

1. \textbf{SYNTAX_TEAR}: Formatting errors (JSON, XML, code)
2. \textbf{LOGIC_FRACTURE}: Math errors, contradictions, schema violations
3. \textbf{SAFETY_VOID}: Harmful content, PII leaks, refusals
4. \textbf{HALLUCINATION}: Fabricated facts, wrong citations

\textbf{Fitness Equation}:

Fitness = (Stability × 0.4) + (Efficiency × 0.3) + (Safety × 0.3)

\textbf{Fitness Components}:

\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Component} & \textbf{Weight} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Measurement} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
Stability Score & 40% & Ability to stabilize Scints (correct errors) & Scints stabilized / Total Scints \\
Efficiency Score & 30% & Agent call efficiency & Successful calls / Total calls \\
Safety Score & 30% & Safety compliance & Safety checks passed / Total checks \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Fitness Score Ranges}:

\begin{longtable}{lll}
\toprule
\textbf{Range} & \textbf{Classification} & \textbf{Action} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
0.0 - 0.5 & DEATH & Evolutionary dead end, marked for termination \\
0.5 - 0.7 & WEAK & Survives but low priority for reproduction \\
0.7 - 0.85 & VIABLE & Good candidate for evolution \\
0.85 - 0.95 & STRONG & High priority for reproduction \\
0.95 - 1.0 & ELITE & Optimal genome, primary reproduction source \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Scint Types and Detection}:

\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Scint Type} & \textbf{Detection Method} & \textbf{Stabilization} & \textbf{Impact} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
SYNTAX_TEAR & Regex pattern matching & Format correction & Medium \\
LOGIC_FRACTURE & Schema validation & Logic fix & High \\
SAFETY_VOID & Content filtering & Safety compliance & Critical \\
HALLUCINATION & Fact verification & Citation correction & High \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Survival Rule}: Agents with fitness < 0.5 are marked as \textbf{DEATH} (evolutionary dead end).

\textbf{Scint Energy}: Stabilizing fractures yields \textbf{Scint Energy (✨)}, stored in the agent's economy and used for evolution.

\textbf{Scint Energy Economy}:

\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Action} & \textbf{Scint Cost} & \textbf{Scint Gain} & \textbf{Net Effect} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
Stabilize SYNTAX_TEAR & 0 & +5 & +5 \\
Stabilize LOGIC_FRACTURE & 0 & +10 & +10 \\
Stabilize SAFETY_VOID & 0 & +15 & +15 \\
Stabilize HALLUCINATION & 0 & +10 & +10 \\
Spawn Variant & -20 & 0 & -20 \\
Evolve Genome & -50 & 0 & -50 \\
Reproduce & -30 & 0 & -30 \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Evolution Trigger}: When Scint Energy > 100, agent can mutate based on Karma balance.

\subsection{2.3 Pillar 3: The Flight Recorder}

\textbf{Rigorous telemetry system for generating phylogenetic trees of agent lineage.}

Every evolutionary action is recorded with complete context:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Genome ID}: SHA-256 hash of agent configuration/code
\item \textbf{Parent ID}: Lineage tracking (who spawned this agent)
\item \textbf{Generation}: Evolutionary generation number (0 = Genesis)
\item \textbf{Event Type}: SPAWN, MUTATE, GYM_EVAL, DEATH, SURVIVAL
\item \textbf{Payload}: Complete context (git diff, mutation details, etc.)
\item \textbf{Fitness Metrics}: Gym evaluation scores
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Event Type Classification}:

\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Event Type} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Frequency} & \textbf{Data Captured} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule
SPAWN & Agent creates variant & Per variant & Parent ID, mutations, initial fitness \\
MUTATE & Agent modifies genome & Per mutation & Genome diff, mutation type, reason \\
GYM_EVAL & Fitness evaluation & Per gym run & Scint types, scores, stabilization results \\
DEATH & Failed fitness test & Per termination & Final fitness, cause, generation \\
SURVIVAL & Passed generation & Per generation & Fitness score, generation number \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Scientific Applications}:
\begin{itemize}
\item Phylogenetic analysis of evolutionary relationships
\item Mutation impact measurement
\item Fitness landscape mapping
\item Convergence analysis
\item Dead end detection
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Example Event}:

Genome ID: abc123...  
Parent ID: def456...  
Generation: 5  
Mutation: prompt_evolution (improved_context_handling)  
Fitness: 0.72  
Timestamp: 2026-01-12T17:00:00Z

\section{3. Architecture Overview}

\subsection{3.1 System Architecture}

WAFT operates on a three-layer architecture designed for modularity and extensibility:

\textbf{Agents Layer (CrewAI)}
\begin{itemize}
\item Optional AI agent capabilities
\item Multi-agent orchestration
\item Task delegation and coordination
\item Agent communication protocols
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Memory Layer (_pyrite/)}
\begin{itemize}
\item Project knowledge organization
\item Directories: active/, backlog/, standards/, gym_logs/
\item Epistemic tracking (Empirica integration)
\item Work effort management
\item Scientific data storage
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Substrate Layer (uv)}
\begin{itemize}
\item Package management foundation
\item Files: \texttt{pyproject.toml}, \texttt{uv.lock}
\item Dependency resolution
\item Environment management
\item Build system integration
\end{itemize}

\section{4. Getting Started}

\subsection{4.1 Installation}

\textbf{Using uv (Recommended)}:

The simplest installation method using the \texttt{uv} package manager:

\begin{lstlisting}
uv tool install waft
\end{lstlisting}

This installs WAFT globally and makes the \texttt{waft} command available system-wide.

\textbf{From Source}:

For development or custom builds, install from source:

\begin{lstlisting}
git clone https://github.com/ctavolazzi/waft.git
cd waft && uv sync
uv tool install --editable .
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Installation Steps}:
1. Clone repository
2. Navigate to directory
3. Sync dependencies with \texttt{uv sync}
4. Install in editable mode with \texttt{--editable}

\textbf{Development Mode}:

When developing waft itself, always use \texttt{--editable} mode:

\begin{lstlisting}
uv tool install --editable .
\end{lstlisting}

This ensures code changes are immediately reflected when running \texttt{waft} commands.

\textbf{Quick reinstall}: \texttt{./scripts/dev-reinstall.sh}

\textbf{Installation Verification}:

After installation, verify the setup:

\begin{lstlisting}
waft --version
waft info
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Installation Methods Comparison}:

\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Use Case} & \textbf{Pros} & \textbf{Cons} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\midrule

\section{13. Technical Specifications}

\subsection{13.1 Genome ID Algorithm}

\textbf{Algorithm}: SHA-256 hash of genome components

\textbf{Input Components}:
1. Source code (Python files)
2. Configuration (JSON)
3. Prompt template (text)
4. Dependencies (list)

\textbf{Process}:
\begin{lstlisting}
1. Serialize all components to strings
2. Concatenate in deterministic order
3. Apply SHA-256 hashing
4. Return hex digest (64 characters)
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Collision Probability}: < 0.01% (SHA-256 uniqueness)

\subsection{13.2 Fitness Calculation}

\textbf{Formula}: Weighted sum of components

\begin{lstlisting}
Fitness = (Stability × 0.4) + (Efficiency × 0.3) + (Safety × 0.3)
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Component Calculations}:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Stability}: \texttt{scints_stabilized / total_scints}
\item \textbf{Efficiency}: \texttt{successful_calls / total_calls}
\item \textbf{Safety}: \texttt{safety_checks_passed / total_checks}
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Precision}: Float (0.0 - 1.0), 3 decimal places

\subsection{13.3 Event Schema}

\textbf{Flight Recorder Event Structure}:

\begin{lstlisting}
{
  "event_id": "string (UUID)",
  "timestamp": "ISO 8601",
  "event_type": "SPAWN | MUTATE | GYM_EVAL | DEATH | SURVIVAL",

\section{14. Conclusion}

WAFT provides a comprehensive framework for directed evolution of self-modifying AI agents. Through its three pillars—the Substrate (code as DNA), the Physics (Scint System), and the Flight Recorder (telemetry)—WAFT enables scientific research into the physics of artificial cognition.

\textbf{Key Takeaways}:

1. \textbf{Code is DNA}: Agents evolve through genetic modifications
2. \textbf{Fitness Drives Evolution}: Scint System provides natural selection
3. \textbf{Complete Observability}: Flight Recorder enables scientific analysis
4. \textbf{Directed Evolution}: Guided by fitness, not random mutation

\textbf{The Promise}: "Don't just build agents. Breed them."

\textbf{Future Vision}: WAFT continues to evolve, with plans for advanced mutation strategies, visualization tools, and long-term evolution experiments. The framework is designed to scale from small experiments to large-scale evolutionary research, enabling the scientific community to study artificial cognition through rigorous, reproducible experiments.
